skill.name: design-an-interface
skill.description: Generate multiple radically different interface designs for a module using parallel sub-agents. Use when user wants to design an API, explore interface options, compare module shapes, or mentions "design it twice".
skill.summary: Explore distinct module interfaces, compare their trade-offs, and synthesize the strongest design.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive caused by a fenced Markdown prompt example in SKILL.md. The skill contains guidance only and shows no command execution or malicious intent.

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 28-46 are a fenced Markdown block containing a sub-agent prompt template. The backticks delimit documentation and do not invoke Ruby, a shell, or any command.

content.value_statement: A first interface idea can hide weak assumptions and unnecessary complexity. This skill generates distinct options, compares trade-offs, and helps select or synthesize a stronger design.
actual_capabilities: Gathers the module purpose, callers, operations, constraints, and encapsulation boundaries.
Generates at least three substantially different interface proposals with parallel sub-agents.
Presents each option with signatures, usage examples, hidden complexity, and trade-offs.
Compares designs through simplicity, flexibility, efficiency, depth, and misuse resistance.
Helps combine useful elements from several proposals into a final direction.
limitations: It designs interface shapes but does not implement the selected module.
Parallel generation depends on an environment that supports sub-agents or equivalent task delegation.
Results depend on clear requirements, constraints, and caller needs.
It focuses on software module interfaces, not visual user interface design.

use_cases.title: Shape a Public Library API
use_cases.description: Explore focused, flexible, and common-case interfaces before committing to a public contract.

use_cases.title: Define a Service Boundary
use_cases.description: Compare module boundaries that expose essential operations while hiding storage, caching, or orchestration details.

use_cases.title: Review a Proposed Interface
use_cases.description: Generate alternatives that reveal assumptions and support a concrete design discussion.

prompt_templates.title: Explore a Simple Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Design three different interfaces for [module]. It must support [key operations] for [callers]. Show usage and explain what each option hides.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a small module and known operations.

prompt_templates.title: Design Under Constraints
prompt_templates.prompt: Design interfaces for [module] under these constraints: [constraints]. Include one minimal option, one flexible option, and one optimized for the common case.
prompt_templates.scenario: Balance several technical or compatibility requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Compare an Existing Proposal
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed interface: [description]. Generate three substantially different alternatives. Compare simplicity, depth, efficiency, flexibility, and resistance to misuse in prose.
prompt_templates.scenario: Challenge a design before implementation or public release.

prompt_templates.title: Synthesize a Final Direction
prompt_templates.prompt: Design four interfaces for [module] using distinct paradigms: [paradigms]. Evaluate them against [priorities], then synthesize a final design with explicit trade-offs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Make an advanced architecture decision with competing priorities.

output_examples.input: Design an interface for a notification module used by web handlers and background jobs.
output: The minimal option exposes one send operation and keeps routing, retries, and provider selection internal.
The flexible option accepts delivery policies and supports advanced callers, but creates more opportunities for inconsistent configuration.
The common-case option provides named notification operations and favors discoverability over broad extensibility.

output_examples.input: Compare interface options for a cache that must support local and remote storage.
output: A storage-neutral interface is easiest for callers and hides backend selection.
A capability-based interface supports backend differences but exposes more concepts.
The recommended direction keeps basic operations uniform and offers advanced capabilities through a separate extension.

best_practices: Provide the module purpose, caller types, key operations, and hard constraints before generating designs.
Require each option to differ in structure or priorities, not only in naming.
Evaluate usage examples and misuse risks before selecting or combining proposals.
anti_patterns: Do not accept several proposals that share the same underlying interface shape.
Do not choose an option before comparing its trade-offs with the alternatives.
Do not turn the exercise into implementation planning or effort estimation.

faq.question: Does this skill implement the selected interface?
faq.answer: No. It explores and evaluates interface shapes without writing the implementation.

faq.question: How many designs does it generate?
faq.answer: It requests at least three substantially different designs. Advanced prompts can request more.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the module purpose, callers, key operations, constraints, and details that should remain internal.

faq.question: Can it review an existing API?
faq.answer: Yes. Supply the current proposal and priorities, then request alternatives and a prose comparison.

faq.question: Does it design visual interfaces?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on software module and API interfaces rather than screen layouts or interaction design.

faq.question: Why does it use multiple sub-agents?
faq.answer: Independent prompts encourage meaningful structural differences and reduce attachment to the first design idea.
